symbols.name: test_the_fixture_is_honest
symbols.doc: The scrambled input order matches neither expected sequence (so a stability leak cannot pass), the keys are unique (so both sequences are total), and the key-alphabetical order differs from both expected sequences (so a comparator that quietly sorts by key cannot pass).

symbols.name: test_ascending_has_three_bands_in_spec_order
symbols.doc: §7.4(1b): 'an ascending sort on such a field has THREE bands, in this order: JSON nulls, then everything else by the table, then the absent-key rows.' ("x" is a string, 5 a number: string < number.)

symbols.name: test_descending_keeps_the_absent_band_last
symbols.doc: NULLS LAST is unconditional; only the present values invert.

symbols.name: test_no_sort_field_collapses_to_key_asc
symbols.doc: §7.4(2): a pick with no sort field still carries a total order — MISSING for every row leaves exactly `ORDER BY key ASC`.

symbols.name: test_the_type_ladder
symbols.doc: Object > Array > Boolean > Number > String > Null, each adjacent pair — with the empty TOP-LEVEL array below the whole ladder, null included.

symbols.name: test_the_empty_array_exception_is_top_level_only
symbols.doc: '[[]]'::jsonb < '[null]'::jsonb is FALSE (measured): a NESTED [] follows the plain table (array > null), and only a top-level [] sorts below everything. Over-applying the exception to nested values would be the same class of defect the exception fixed, in the other direction.

symbols.name: test_booleans_are_not_numbers_here
symbols.doc: Python says 0 == False and 1 == True; jsonb_typeof does not. A comparator built on Python equality passes everything else and fails this (§7.2 item 5's trap, in its ordering form).

symbols.name: _panes

symbols.name: test_ac41b_ten_runs_of_one_pick_return_one_sequence

symbols.name: test_ac41c_the_two_panes_sequences_are_equal_element_for_element
